title: 1988 British International Helicopters Sikorsky S-61N crash

route.from_name: Safe Felicia North Sea semi-submersible rig

location.name: North Sea, 29 nm northeast of Sumburgh, Shetland Isles

summary: Sikorsky S-61N helicopter G-BEID, on a charter flight from a North Sea oil platform to Sumburgh with 2 pilots and 19 passengers, experienced a fire in the main gearbox bay after a bearing failure in the No. 2 engine. The crew executed a controlled ditching in the North Sea 11 nm offshore. All 21 occupants successfully evacuated to liferafts and were rescued.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by an uncontrollable fire in the main gearbox bay which probably resulted from the effects of failure of the No. 5 bearing in the No. 2 engine. An underlying factor was the lack of any fire detection or suppression capability within the main gearbox bay. The cause of the bearing failure could not be positively established. (p. 1, 54)

factors.evidence: The No. 5 bearing (Part No. MRC 4003T47P01) in the No. 2 engine power turbine failed, as indicated by the muffled crack or 'bang' heard by the co-pilot and several passengers approximately 5 minutes into the flight. The bearing consisted of 11 balls of 0.5625 inch diameter running on a static outer ring and split inner ring rotating with the PT shaft. (p. 2, 41-44)

Six seconds after the initial bang, the No. 2 engine fire warning lights illuminated. Ninety seconds after the initial noise, the No. 1 engine fire warning lights also illuminated. Passengers observed oil coming from the cabin ceiling and smoke issuing from a joint in the ceiling panels. About 4 minutes after ditching, passengers saw signs of a growing fire at the right side of the main gearbox housing. (p. 2-3, 48-51)

The engine bays were provided with fire detection and extinguishing systems, but such systems were not provided for the main gearbox bay and were not required by the applicable Airworthiness Regulations at that time. The main gearbox bay had no fire detection sensing loops and no fire extinguishing capability. (p. 3, 12, 51)

A gentle power-on ditching was made 11 nm off the Shetland Island Coast at 14:31 UTC, some 30 seconds after the visual confirmation of the fire and 3 minutes after the initial abnormal noise. The co-pilot streamed the sea anchor and the aircraft floated satisfactorily with flotation bags correctly deployed. (p. 3)

All twenty-one occupants evacuated successfully into liferafts. Passengers and crew deployed two 14-man liferafts and were successfully winched into Search and Rescue helicopters. The last survivor was rescued at 1528 hours. (p. 3-4)

events.text: Helicopter G-BEID departed the Safe Felicia semi-submersible oil platform with two pilots and a full passenger load of 19 for a one-hour charter return flight to Sumburgh.

Aircraft at 40 nm from Sumburgh and 15 nm from Shetland Island coast, cruising on Track J at 1,500 feet altitude in Instrument Meteorological Conditions, established radio telephony contact with Sumburgh Approach ATC.

Co-pilot (handling pilot) heard a muffled crack or 'bang' from the area of the No. 2 engine drive train, also heard by a number of passengers. Both crew felt a slight change in the vibratory feel of the aircraft.

Approximately 6 seconds after the bang, No. 2 engine fire warning lights illuminated brightly. Engine instrument checks revealed nothing unusual and no visible signs of smoke or fire were observed by the crew.
Co-pilot started descent in accordance with Engine Fire in Flight Drill. Commander retarded No. 2 engine speed select lever to ground idle and started a stopwatch.
Mayday distress call transmitted at 14:28:44 on Sumburgh ATC Approach frequency, reporting an engine fire (incorrectly identifying it as No. 1) and intention to descend to 500 feet and continue VFR.
About 48 seconds after the bang, No. 2 engine was shut down by operation of the Fire Emergency Shut-Off Selector handle and the main fire extinguisher fired in accordance with Emergency Drill Step B.

Approximately 90 seconds after the initial noise, No. 1 engine fire warning lights also illuminated. No. 2 engine fire warning lights remained illuminated. Passengers observed oil streaking down cabin trim panels and smoke issuing from ceiling panels.
Co-pilot increased rate of descent, breaking cloud at 800 feet and leveling at low height using automatic Low Altitude Warning System voice alerts.
Commander took aircraft controls and briefed passengers via cabin public address system to prepare for emergency ditching. Co-pilot deployed floats and made a 'ditching' radio call.
Co-pilot put head out of cockpit window to check float deployment and observed a great deal of smoke behind the aircraft, confirming fire.
Gentle power-on ditching was made 11 nm off the Shetland Island Coast. The aircraft floated satisfactorily with flotation bags correctly deployed. By this time the cabin had filled with smoke.
Post-ditching procedures executed. Commander shut down No. 1 engine and instructed co-pilot to open cabin door. Co-pilot deployed forward liferaft and donned immersion suit.
Rotors running down (took approximately 2 minutes). Rear liferaft launched and passenger evacuation began. Co-pilot entered smoke-filled cabin to assist passengers.

Approximately 4 minutes after ditching, passengers in the forward liferaft saw signs of a growing fire at the right side of the main gearbox housing. Crew and passengers paddled liferafts away from the burning aircraft and linked them together.
Search and Rescue helicopter FK arrived overhead at 14:36 UTC and reported helicopter floating upright with liferafts deployed. Rescue 117 SAR helicopter arrived at scene at 14:59 UTC.
After lifting 14 of the liferaft occupants, Rescue 117 was required to dump fuel before lifting the remaining 7 occupants. Rescue 117 arrived at Sumburgh with all survivors at 15:49 UTC.

recommendations.text: Enhance fire detection and suppression systems in the main gearbox bay of S-61N helicopters.
Review and improve bearing condition monitoring procedures for power turbine No. 5 bearings in CT58 engines.
Implement magnetic chip detector (MCD) inspection procedures with specific guidance for debris found during 50-hour inspections.
Establish mandatory procedures for Installed Engine Vibration Checks after power turbine module or drive train component replacement.

safety_changes: Installation of fire detection and suppression systems in main gearbox bays on S-61N helicopters.
Enhanced bearing monitoring and inspection procedures for power turbine bearings.
Improved maintenance documentation for magnetic chip detector inspection and interpretation.
Mandatory vibration checks after certain drive train maintenance operations.
Enhanced crew training for fire detection and emergency procedures in multi-engine helicopters.
